Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 60, verses 1–9:

It is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Many of the exegetes, may Allah have mercy on them, mention that the occasion of revelation of these noble verses concerns the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) set out on the expedition of the Conquest. Hatib wrote to the polytheists of Makkah informing them of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) march toward them, seeking thereby to gain a favour with them, not out of doubt or hypocrisy. He sent the letter with a woman, but the Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of his affair, so he sent after the woman before she arrived, took the letter from her, and rebuked Hatib. Hatib offered an excuse, and the Prophet (ﷺ) accepted it.

These verses contain a severe prohibition against taking the disbelievers, both polytheists and others, as allies and extending affection to them, and that this contradicts faith and opposes the creed of Abraham the Friend (peace be upon him), and contradicts reason, which requires the utmost caution against an enemy who spares no effort in enmity and seizes every opportunity to inflict harm upon his foe.

{1} Allah, the Exalted, says: {O you who have believed}; that is: act according to the requirements of your faith, by allying with whoever stands by faith and opposing whoever opposes it. For they are an enemy of Allah and an enemy of the believers. So {do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending affection to them}; that is: do not hasten to love them and strive for the causes of that love. For when affection is established, support and alliance follow it, and the servant departs from faith and becomes one of the people of disbelief [and is cut off from the people of faith]. Moreover, the one who takes a disbeliever as an ally is also devoid of manliness, for how can he ally with the greatest of his enemies, who wants nothing for him but evil, and oppose his Lord and Protector, who wants good for him and commands and urges him to it? Another thing that calls the believer to oppose the disbelievers is that they have disbelieved in the truth that came to the believers, and there is no greater opposition and hostility than this. For they have disbelieved in the foundation of your religion and claimed that you are misguided and upon no guidance, while in fact they have disbelieved in the truth about which there is no doubt. Whoever rejects the truth, it is impossible that there be any proof or argument to support his claim. Indeed, mere knowledge of the truth proves the falsehood and corruption of the one who rejects it.

And among their intense enmity is that they {expel the Messenger and you}: O believers, from your homes, and drive you out from your lands, though you have no fault in their eyes except that you believe {in Allah, your Lord}: the One whom all creation is obliged to worship, because He nurtured them and bestowed upon them blessings, both apparent and hidden [and He is Allah, the Exalted]. When they turned away from this matter, which is the most obligatory of obligations, and you upheld it, they became hostile to you and expelled you from your homes because of it. What religion, what manliness, and what reason remains with the servant who allies with disbelievers whose description is this in every time and place, and nothing restrains him from that except fear or a strong obstacle? {If you have gone out to strive in My way and seek My pleasure}; that is: if your departure was intended for jihad in the way of Allah, to raise the word of Allah and seek His good pleasure, then act according to what this requires, by allying with the friends of Allah and opposing His enemies, for this is among the greatest jihad in His way and among the greatest means by which those who draw near to Allah seek His pleasure. {You secretly send them affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you reveal}; that is: how can you secretly send affection to the disbelievers and conceal it, while you know that Allah knows what you conceal and what you disclose? Though it may be hidden from the believers, it is not hidden from Allah, the Exalted, and He will recompense the servants for what He knows of them of good and evil. {And whoever of you does it}; that is: allies with the disbelievers after Allah has warned you against it, {has certainly strayed from the right path}, because he has taken a course contrary to the Sharia, to reason, and to human manliness.

{2} Then He, the Exalted, explains the severity of their enmity, to stir the believers against them: {If they overcome you}; that is: if they find you and an opportunity to harm you presents itself, {they will be enemies to you}: openly, {and extend against you their hands}: with killing, striking, and the like, {and their tongues with evil}; that is: with speech that offends, such as insult and other things, {and they wish that you would disbelieve}: for this is the utmost of what they want from you.

{3} If you argue and say: we ally with the disbelievers for the sake of kinship and wealth, then your wealth and your children will not avail you anything against Allah. {And Allah is Seeing of what you do}; therefore He warns you against allying with the disbelievers, whose alliance harms you.

{4} {Indeed} there was {for you}, O company of believers, {an excellent example}; that is: a good model and a beneficial pattern to follow {in Abraham and those with him}: of the believers, for you have been commanded to follow the creed of Abraham, a hanif. {When they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah"}; that is: when Abraham, peace be upon him, and those with him among the believers disassociated themselves from their polytheist people and from what they worshipped besides Allah. Then they declared their enmity in the clearest terms, saying: {We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred}; that is: appeared and become manifest. Hatred in the hearts and the cessation of affection, and enmity in the bodies. This enmity and hatred have no time limit or boundary, but rather it is {forever} as long as you remain persistent in your disbelief, {until you believe in Allah alone}; that is: when you believe in Allah alone, the enmity and hatred cease, and turn into affection and alliance. So for you, O believers, there is an excellent example in Abraham and those with him in standing firm upon faith and monotheism and what follows from them and their requirements, and in everything they worshipped Allah alone in. {Except}: in one matter, which is: {the saying of Abraham to his father}: Azar, the polytheist, disbelieving, obstinate one, when he invited him to faith and monotheism and he refused. Abraham said to him: {I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power to benefit you against Allah at all}: but I supplicate to my Lord, perhaps I will not be wretched through the supplication of my Lord. So you are not to follow Abraham in this state in which he prayed for the polytheist. You are not to pray for the polytheists and say: we in that are following the creed of Abraham, for Allah has mentioned Abraham's excuse in that by His saying: {And the request of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to Abraham that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him...} the verse. And for you there is an excellent example in Abraham and those with him when they called upon Allah, relied upon Him, turned to Him in repentance, and acknowledged their incapacity and shortcoming, saying: {Our Lord, upon You we have relied}; that is: we have depended upon You to bring what benefits us and to repel what harms us, and we have trusted You, O our Lord, in that. {And to You we have turned in repentance}; that is: we have returned to Your obedience and Your pleasure and everything that brings us near to You. So we strive in that, diligent in doing good deeds, and we know that to You is the final return, so we shall prepare for coming before You and do what brings us near to You.

{5} {Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers}; that is: do not empower them over us because of our sins, so that they tempt us and prevent us from what they are able to prevent of matters of faith, and so that they also are tempted by themselves, for when they see that they have the upper hand, they think that they are upon the truth and that we are upon falsehood, and so they increase in disbelief and transgression. {And forgive us}: for what we have committed of sins and misdeeds and what we have fallen short of in obligations. {Our Lord, indeed You are the Exalted in Might}: the Subduer of everything. {the Wise}: who places things in their proper places. So by Your might and Your wisdom, grant us victory over our enemies, forgive us our sins, and set right our faults.

{6} Then He repeated the exhortation to them to follow their example, saying: {There has certainly been for you in them an excellent example}: and not every person finds this example easy, but it is easy for the one {who hopes for Allah and the Last Day}. For faith and the expectation of reward and recompense make every hardship easy for the servant and make every great thing seem small to him, and they cause him [to increase in] following the righteous servants of Allah, the prophets and the messengers, for he sees himself as in need of that and compelled to it to the utmost degree of compulsion. {And whoever turns away}: from obedience to Allah and following the messengers of Allah, {will not harm except himself, and does not harm Allah at all}. {Indeed, Allah is the Free of need}: who possesses complete and absolute independence from every aspect, so He has no need of any of His creatures in any way. {the Praiseworthy}: in His essence [and His names], attributes, and actions, for He is praised for all of that.

{7} Then Allah, the Exalted, informed that this enmity which Allah commanded the believers to hold toward the polytheists, and which He described them as upholding, applies as long as they remain in their polytheism and disbelief. If they transfer to faith, the ruling revolves with its cause, and the affection of faith returns. So do not despair, O believers, of their return to faith: {Perhaps Allah will bring about between you and those whom you have taken as enemies a bond of affection}: the cause of which will be their return to faith. {And Allah is Competent}: over everything, and among that is guiding hearts and turning them from one state to another. {And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful}: no sin is too great for Him to forgive, and no fault too burdensome for Him to conceal. {Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"}. In this verse there is an indication and a glad tiding of the conversion to Islam of some of the polytheists, who were at that time enemies of the believers, and this has indeed occurred, and all praise and favour belong to Allah.

{8} When these noble verses, which stir enmity toward the disbelievers, were revealed, they had their full effect upon the believers, who upheld them to the utmost, and they regarded as sinful maintaining ties with some of their polytheist relatives, thinking that this fell within what Allah had forbidden. So Allah informed them that this does not fall within what is prohibited, saying: {Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes—from being righteous to them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly}; that is: Allah does not forbid you from righteousness, kinship, reciprocating with kindness, and acting justly toward the polytheists among your relatives and others, so long as they are not in a state of arraying themselves to fight you over religion and to expel you from your homes. There is no blame upon you in maintaining ties with them, for maintaining ties with them in this state carries no harm and no consequence, as Allah, the Exalted, said regarding disbelieving parents when their child is Muslim: {And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness}.

{9} As for His saying: {Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over religion}; that is: because of your religion, in enmity to the religion of Allah and to those who uphold it, {and expel you from your homes and aid [others] in your expulsion}; that is: assist others {in expelling you}: Allah forbids you {from taking them as allies}: by support and affection, in word and deed. As for your righteousness and kindness that do not amount to alliance with the polytheists, Allah has not forbidden you from it, rather that falls within the general command to be kind to relatives and others among the children of Adam and beyond. {And whoever takes them as allies} from among you, {those are the wrongdoers}: and that wrongdoing is according to the degree of alliance. If it is complete alliance, it is disbelief that takes one out of the fold of Islam, and beneath that are degrees, some severe and some lesser.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 60, verses 10–11:**

{10} When the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah took place, the Prophet (ﷺ) agreed with the polytheists that whoever came to the Muslims from among them as a Muslim would be returned to the polytheists. This was a general and unrestricted term, and its generality included both women and men. As for the men, God did not forbid His Messenger from returning them to the disbelievers, in fulfilment of the condition and to complete the treaty, which is among the greatest of benefits. As for the women, since returning them involved many harms, He commanded the believers: when ﴿believing women come to you as emigrants﴾, and you doubt the sincerity of their faith, then test and examine them with what shows their sincerity, such as strong oaths and other means. For it is possible that their faith is not sincere, but rather that they desire a husband, a land, or some other worldly aim. If they are of this description, then their return is required, in fulfilment of the condition and without any resulting harm. But if they test them and find them sincere, or they know this about them without testing, then they must not return them to the disbelievers. ﴿They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾: this is a great harm [in returning them], which the Lawgiver (al-Shari', the divine lawgiver) took into account. He also took into account the fulfilment of the condition, by giving the disbelievers their husbands' equivalent of what they had spent on the women, namely the dower (mahr) and its related expenses, as compensation for them. In that case, there is no blame upon the Muslims if they marry these women, even if they had husbands in the land of polytheism, provided they give them their due compensation of dower and maintenance. Just as a Muslim woman is not lawful to a disbeliever, so a disbelieving woman is not lawful to a Muslim [to keep] as long as she remains in disbelief, except for the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab). For this reason, God the Exalted said: ﴿And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women﴾. If holding on to their marriage bond is forbidden, then forbidding initiating a marriage with them is even more fitting. ﴿And ask for what you have spent﴾: O believers, when your wives go back as apostates to the disbelievers, then if the disbelievers take from the Muslims the expenses of the women among them who have become Muslim, the Muslims are entitled to take in exchange what was lost of their wives to the disbelievers.

In this there is evidence that the departure of the marital bond (bud') from the husband has value. Therefore, if someone spoils a man's marriage to a woman, by fostering or otherwise, he is liable for the dower.

As for His saying ﴿That is the judgment of God﴾: that is, this ruling which God has mentioned and made clear to you is the judgment of God; He has explained it to you and clarified it. ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: He knows what rulings are suitable for you, and He legislates them according to His wisdom and mercy.

{11} As for His saying ﴿And if any of your wives escape to the disbelievers﴾: by their going forth as apostates, ﴿and then you gain a victory [over them], give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾: as has already been mentioned, if the disbelievers were taking from the Muslims in exchange for what was lost of their wives to the Muslims, then whoever among the Muslims has a wife who goes over to the disbelievers and is lost to him, the Muslims must give him from the spoils of war (ghanima) the equivalent of what he spent. ﴿And fear God, in whom you are believers﴾: your faith in God requires that you be constant in piety at all times.

This is the commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 60, verse 12:

{12} These conditions mentioned in this verse are called the pledge of allegiance of women (mubayaʿat al-nisaʾ), which women used to pledge to uphold the common obligations that are binding upon both men and women at all times. As for men, what is obligatory upon them varies according to their circumstances, ranks, and what is specifically incumbent upon them. The Prophet (ﷺ) would carry out what Allah commanded him [with regard to it]. So when women came to him pledging allegiance and committing themselves to these conditions, he would accept their pledge, comfort their hearts, and ask Allah to forgive them for whatever shortcomings occurred from them, and he would include them among the believers. {On condition that they do not associate anything with Allah}: rather, they should single out Allah alone for worship. {And that they do not kill their children}: as was practiced by the ignorant women of the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah). {And that they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse}: as was widespread among prostitutes and those who take secret lovers. {And that they do not bring forth a slander which they have invented between their hands and their feet}: and "buhtan" means fabricating falsehood against others; that is, they should not fabricate falsehood in any situation, whether it concerns their husbands or concerns others. {And that they do not disobey you in what is right}; that is, they should not disobey you in any matter you command them, because your command is never except in what is right. Among this is their obedience to you in forbidding wailing (niyahah), tearing one's garments, scratching faces, and calling out with the cries of the Jahiliyyah. {Then accept their pledge}: when they commit to all that has been mentioned. {And ask Allah's forgiveness for them}: for their shortcomings, and to console their hearts. {Indeed, Allah is Forgiving}; that is, abundantly forgiving toward the disobedient and bountiful in kindness toward the sinners who repent. {Merciful}: His mercy encompasses everything, and His kindness has reached all creatures.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 60, verse 13:

{13} Meaning: O you who believe, if you truly believe in your Lord, follow His pleasure, and keep away from His anger, {do not take as allies a people with whom God is angry}: He is angry with them only because of their disbelief, and this covers all categories of disbelievers. {They have despaired of the Hereafter}; that is, they have been deprived of the good of the Hereafter, so they have no share in it. So beware of taking them as allies, lest you agree with them in their evil and their polytheism and thus be deprived of the good of the Hereafter as they have been deprived. As for His saying: {as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves}: when they arrive at the Abode of the Hereafter, witness the reality of the matter, and know with certainty that they have no share in it.
It is also possible that the meaning is: they have despaired of the Hereafter, that is, they have denied it and disbelieved in it; then it is not strange that they would proceed to what displeases God and to the causes of His punishment. Their despair of the Hereafter is like the despair of the disbelievers who deny resurrection in this world concerning the return of those in the graves to God, exalted is He.

The tafsir is complete. And God knows best.
